materials/bronze: "does not spark when struck, making it safer near flammable gases": non-sparking hand gear is usually specified in aluminium bronze or beryllium copper; true of copper alloys generally, but not a standard selling point of every tin bronze
"is used for ship propellers because it resists seawater": large propellers are mostly nickel-aluminium bronze; the traditional 'manganese bronze' is metallurgically a brass
materials/cement: "is responsible for about eight percent of global carbon dioxide emissions": published estimates range roughly 5 to 8 percent depending on year and whether energy use is counted

"was patented by an English bricklayer early in the nineteenth century": Joseph Aspdin, 1824, is usually described as a bricklayer or mason; his product differed from modern high-temperature Portland cement
materials/granite: "makes up a large part of the continental crust": true of granitic rocks broadly (granite, granodiorite); strict granite alone is a smaller share
"shows coarse, visible crystals speckled black, white and pink": pink appears only where potassium feldspar is pink; many granites are grey and white
materials/plastic: "was first produced fully synthetically early in the twentieth century": Bakelite (1907, patented 1909) is conventionally the first fully synthetic plastic; semi-synthetic celluloid is older
materials/wood: "frames most new houses built in North America": true for single-family houses in the US and Canada; less so for multi-storey housing
